_comment: sCure version registry - newest first. On every release: bump the VERSION file at the repo root AND add an entry here (version, date, notes). The Settings > Versions modal shows this list.

notes: Temperature-sensor supervision: an NTC reading open-circuit (3.3 V pull-up rail) for 60 s raises a registry alert - 9001 TEMP_SENSOR_DISCONNECTED (critical) for the required chamber / Left LED / Right LED sensors, 9050 LED_TEMP_SENSOR_DISCONNECTED (warning) for the Back / Door LED sensors. Checked at start-up, every second by the status loop, and right before every process start (3 reads 0.5 s apart) - a process is refused with code 9001 while a required sensor is open; Back / Door open only warns, processes run as usual. /api/state now carries sensors {} and alerts []; the UI raises registry codes published by the hardware service
errors.json 9001 / 9050 added; SRS 7.4 'Temperature-sensor supervision' + registry rows; QA: sensor policy mirror + /api/state sensors/alerts test

Cure history indication: every telemetry post notes which temperature sensors read open-circuit; at finish the run record gets sensorIssues [{sensor, critical}] (JSON store + Postgres cure_runs.sensor_issues, v_cure_history). History rows show 'Sensor disconnected during run: Back LED, Door LED' (red when a required sensor was involved) and the cure report gets a 'Temperature Sensors' card

Program totalDuration now IS the estimated real length (holds + heating ramps + cooling, program-estimate.ts): stored on save from the program builder and on CSV import, and the built-in presets were recomputed (demo-data.ts + server/db/seed_presets.sql, e.g. ST45 35 -> 79 min because the 60 -> 25 C medium cooling alone takes ~23 min). Builder footer shows 'holds' and '~total' side by side
SRS §6.5 Cure time, §6.7 footer / Save Program and CSV import naming updated with the measured-rate model

Program time estimates re-based on the MEASURED phase timings (141 records collected on the test machine 2026-08-12 .. 2026-09-07, reviewed 2026-09-07): new src/lib/program-estimate.ts - heating ramp 13 s/C up to 45 C, 50 s/C from 45 to 75 C, 80 s/C above (was a flat 2 s/C in the simulation); cooling 1.5 C/min medium, 2.5 fast (measured; was 2.5 / 5), slow 0.8 interpolated (was 1) - the 0.4 C/min runs of 08-31/09-01 were the damper short-travel bug, not slow mode

Home page material list and the CSV builder now show the estimated REAL program length (holds + ramps + cooling, '~N min'); the cure page overall progress uses the same estimate instead of the hold minutes only; the off-Pi ramp/cooling simulation follows the measured rates
Phase-timing records now also carry coolingMode, intensity and timerMode (server/app.py + reportPhaseTiming) so the next review can separate cooling modes and UV loads
QA: 'Program Estimate Mirror' test (heating bands, cooling rates, a worked program)

Wavelength turn-on order: the LED_SWITCH relay (TCA P05 -> K4) is driven to the mode's position FIRST, verified, and given switch_settle_sec (components.json led_power, default 0.1 s, applied only when the relay actually moved) before the SSR enables / GPIO17 are raised and the DIM PWM is written - apply_led_power() reordered and it also enforces the settle since the relay's LAST move on every power-up, so a Cure -> Bleaching transition (relay parked to 0 inside the all-LEDs-off step) waits too. Logged as 'LED_SWITCH relay -> N (mode)' / 'LED_SWITCH relay settled (X ms since it moved)'
QA: 'LED Turn-On Order' mirror test

LED_SWITCH relay (TCA6424A P05 -> Q28 -> K4, LED_OUT1/LED_OUT2 at J21) is now the wavelength router: components.json led_power.modes.<mode>.led_switch = 1 for Cure / 405nm, 0 for Bleaching / 450nm; SystemController._set_led_switch() drives + verifies it on every select_mode() and apply_led_power(), and parks it at 0 at rest (startup, led_power_off, shutdown)
HSI sCure (3).xlsx: LED_SWITCH, WAVELENGTH_ROUTING-GPIO17 and WAVELENGTH_MODE rows updated to the bench-verified behavior (backup copy kept next to it)
QA: 'LED Routing Table Mirror' extended with the led_switch column

Wavelength switch parked in the 405nm position at startup: SystemController.startup_safe() now drives GPIO17 per the default mode's routing table right after the safe-state reset (read-back verified, logged), so the machine never idles in the 450 switch position that cuts the door LED-driver DIM rail (bench 2026-09-07)
pi-setup.sh: adds gpio=16,17,20=op,dl to /boot/firmware/config.txt (idempotent) so the SSR enables and the switch are driven LOW by the firmware from power-on until scure.service starts

LED_SWITCH relay (TCA6424A P05 -> Q28 -> K4, LED_OUT1/LED_OUT2 at J21) parked at 0 on every safe path: TCA all_safe(), startup_safe() (verified + logged) and the API shutdown hook (together with SSR/switch GPIOs LOW). The chip powers up as inputs with pull-ups, so the net floated HIGH (relay engaged) from power-on until the API started
New scripts/scure-io-safe.service + io-safe-boot.sh (installed by pi-setup.sh): seconds after boot, before scure.service, drives GPIO16/17/20 LOW and the TCA P05 output to 0
QA: 'Startup Wavelength Switch Position' mirror test (switch LOW, LED_SWITCH 0, firmware gpio line)
RGB status strip: a running cure/bleaching program shows a PURPLE comet again (components.json rgb.status.busy = purple; it had been yellow, which read the same as the door/idle colors on the bench)

RGB status colors (normal/fault/door_open/busy/no_internet/manual_heat/brightness) are re-read from components.json about once a second (StatusLeds._reload_colors), so color edits apply live without a service restart
Fix: POST /api/rgb (manual strip override) returned HTTP 500 - IOBridge had no set_rgb(); implemented (solid color while on, automatic colors pause and repaint on release)
QA: 'RGB Strip Override Release' endpoint test; RGB status logic test text updated to the purple comet

Bleaching fix: the door LED never received its DIM signal in 450nm mode. Bench-proven on testingcm5 (PCA9685 LED12 register identical in both modes; door DIM measured 0 V whenever the wavelength-routing line GPIO17 was HIGH, 12 V with GPIO17 LOW + 450nm SSR only) - the assumed HIGH=450nm polarity was inverted. components.json led_power.modes.450nm.routing is now 0 (both modes keep GPIO17 LOW; the SSRs alone select the wavelength), the comment records the finding, flow diagram updated

io_controller: led_power (SSR/routing GPIOs, mode table, min_intensity, led_max_duty) is now re-read from components.json live (SystemController.lp property, at most once per second, like heater_cfg) so config fixes take effect without a service restart; falls back to the last good table
QA: 'LED Routing Table Mirror' test (both wavelength modes keep routing=0, SSR table 450=GPIO16 only / 405=GPIO16+GPIO20)

DVT: two-page campaign overview (dvt_tool/overview.py -> DVT/docs/DVT_Overview.pdf, A4, English: key figures, what the DVT proves, phases and gates, units, method rules, instrumentation, console, status, decisions needed) and a Word edition (dvt_tool/overview_docx.py -> DVT_Overview.docx) with one heading per test grouped by phase, so the test list reads from the headings / navigation pane; python-docx added to requirements

DVT console: Git checkpoints (dvt_tool/checkpoint.py) — Reports → 'Save checkpoint to Git…' and automatically when a phase gate (TRR) is signed: the campaign is exported and a snapshot (campaign JSON, workbook, report, CHECKPOINT.md with who/when/progress per machine) is committed under DVT/checkpoints/<campaign>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>_<label>/ as one commit, pushed when a remote exists; only that folder is committed; toggles for push and auto-checkpoint
QA: 'Git Checkpoint Naming + Commit Message' mirror test; pytest: checkpoint in a temporary repository (files, commit message, dirty tree untouched, second checkpoint, no-repo error)

DVT console: several people work on one campaign through the Google Drive folder, no server (dvt_tool/journal.py) — each console appends its writes to its own journal file in <folder>/journal/, pulls the others' every 15 s and replays them into its local campaign.db (idempotent by uuid, timestamp order); a run belongs to whoever started it first (later claims are reported as conflicts and overridden on every console); attachments copied to <folder>/attachments/<run>/; ids of redlines / waivers / supplementary runs / NCRs re-used on replay; machine address, language, meter and SSH settings stay local; a new PC bootstraps the whole campaign from the folder
DVT Settings: 'Shared campaign (team)' card — folder, this console's id, other consoles, event counts, Pull now; toasts for team updates and claim conflicts
QA: 'Team Journal Merge (Drive folder)' mirror test; pytest: two consoles sharing, third-console bootstrap, first-claim-wins, local-only settings

DVT console: the machine address is also the SSH host — new 'SSH access' card on the DUT page (host from the address, user testingpi and key ~/.ssh/scure_pi by default, remembered in the campaign store) with Open SSH terminal, Test SSH (BatchMode hostname / IP / uptime) and Copy command; the simulator has no SSH host
DVT console: the saved machine is the real unit again (http://192.168.2.155:3001) instead of the simulator
QA: 'DUT Address Doubles As SSH Host' mirror test; pytest: ssh host / command helpers

DVT catalog v0.21: DVT-THM-001 gains the 100 V low-line rows (30 °C and 80 °C on the 110 V selector position — 83 % of the 110 V heater power, the longest heat-up and hardest REQ-48 point); AC source now 100 / 110 / 230 / 240 V; 12 matrix rows, +10 runs; 207 V (230 V side) stays a CONFIRM

DVT process figures are now engineering sheets in English only: header (project, test id + title, base state / step), ISO 7200-style title block (project, document, test, step, catalog revision, date, sheet, drawn), legend and tag key in the title block, component reference designators on the drawing (F1/F2 fuses, K1/K2 SSRs, E1 heater, M1-M7 fans, RT1-RT6 thermistors, TC1/TC2 thermocouples, SV1 N2 valve, QE1/QE2 O2 probes, H1-H4 LED panels, A1 controller, G1 PSU, X1 inlet, HMI), 'top view · not to scale' note; the drawing stays English in the Hebrew console (only the card title is translated) and the Hebrew figure translations were removed
DVT docs/figures/*.svg re-exported as the new sheets (test title + catalog revision in the title block)

DVT campaign document (SRS-DVT-197): Reports → 'Campaign document (PDF)' writes one HTML document and prints it to PDF with the installed Chrome / Edge (headless), in the console's language (Hebrew RTL, identifiers LTR) — cover with counts, contents, units, phases with gates and bench order, thresholds with CONFIRM marks, campaign status (progress, verdict matrix, NCRs, waivers, temperature by component), every test in bench order with its process figure, purpose, sample rationale, safety plan, sweep / cases, equipment (+ calibration ids), preconditions, procedure with the fields each step records, data fields, pass criteria, the catalog's CONFIRM lines and the runs recorded so far, and the list of every open CONFIRM decision

DVT: the document lands in the export folder (so the next sync puts it on Drive), is logged as a campaign event and opened; also from the shell: python -m dvt_tool.docgen --lang he; dvt_tool/docgen.py (DocBuilder, confirm_items, find_browser); SRS-DVT-Tool requirement 197, compliance row, README; pytest builds the EN + HE documents and the PDF; QA mirror test

DVT bench order (SRS-DVT-196): tests that use the same instrument now run one after the other — every equipment entry is reduced to an instrument (PicoLog TC-08, Ophir StarBright, O2 analyser, AC source, thermal camera, …; fuses, links and break-out leads are not instruments) and inside each phase the tests are ordered greedily to keep the current bench setup (most shared instruments, fewest new ones, then catalog order); in-phase dependencies and the earth-first / destructive-last rules always win — e.g. Phase 2 runs Ophir (SAF-012, SAF-007) → SAF-014 → the TC-08 heater-body block (SAF-004, 005, 003, 013, 015 …) → the O2-analyser block (GAS-002…006)

DVT Test Console: the unit's next action follows the bench order and prefers the test that keeps the instruments of the unit's last finished test; a 🔧 line says what stays on the bench, what to add and what to remove
DVT Test Plans: each phase is shown as instrument groups (🔧 PicoLog TC-08, Thermocouples … → the tests that share that setup)

DVT: dvt_tool/bench.py (pure logic), SRS-DVT-Tool requirement 196, compliance row, plan doc §4 rule 4, README; pytest: instrument mapping, dependency-first grouping, next action keeps the setup; QA: 'DVT Bench Order · Same Instrument, One Test After The Other' mirror test

DVT catalog v0.20: new Nitrogen subsystem, DVT-GAS-002…008 — inlet over-pressure 1.0/1.5/2.0x rated with the valve closed and open (no N2 past a closed valve, chamber pressure / door seal, valve leak-tight after), supply low/lost (enable guard, pre-cure check, mid-purge, mid-cure), valve fail-safe (off 24 h, power loss, door, abort), venting before job complete / door release, room O2 at the operator, solenoid coil temperature; nitrogen_thresholds block (CONFIRM limits block the tests until set); 38 tests / 457 runs
DVT console: Process subsystem added to the navigation rail; any *_thresholds block in the catalog is now available to pass_criteria
DVT docs: plan rows, method note and open issues 26-28 — no N2 line-pressure sensor on the board (n2LinePressure null) and the Settings guard (null < 6) blocks nitrogen mode on real hardware
QA: 'DVT-GAS-003 · Nitrogen Line Pressure In Telemetry' readiness test and the N2 fault family in the error-registry coverage test

DVT catalog v0.19: new test DVT-GAS-001 — nitrogen purge: time to 95 % N2 (oxygen analyser at the chamber centre + worst corner, 95 % N2 = O2 <= 4.8 %) and how long the chamber holds above 95 % N2 once the valve closes; chamber at ambient and at 80 C (the cure condition), 2 reps, every unit — 32 tests / 427 runs; new 'Process' subsystem (colour, icon, Hebrew label)

DVT-GAS-001 criteria: 95 % reached, valve closed confirmed, damper closed + extraction off during the purge, time to 95 % <= nitrogen_thresholds.purge_time_max_s, programmed purge time >= 1.2x the measured time on this unit, hold >= nitrogen_thresholds.hold_time_min_s, and the hold must cover the longest UV cure that follows a purge (the machine closes the valve after the fixed purge and cures on what is left); thresholds are CONFIRM (null -> BLOCKED); N2 consumption and O2 rise rate recorded

DVT: new nitrogen_thresholds block exposed to pass criteria; Hebrew overlay, verification plan (phase row, table, New in Rev B, open decision 28), README; pytest criteria test; QA readiness test 'DVT-GAS-001 · Nitrogen Purge Is Time-Based (no O2 feedback)' — expected finding: /api/state has nitrogenActive but no oxygen reading, so the Settings purge duration (default 120 s) must be set from the worst unit's measured time

DVT: process figures — every test now has a schematic on the wizard overview page and on each procedure step: top view of the chamber (four LED panels with thermistors and fans, heater with control NTC and TC-08 bond, thermal cutout, circulation/intake fans, door with sensor and lock), the mains chain (inlet, 15 A inlet fuse, voltage selector with its actual position, 5 A heater fuse, SSRs, LED drivers, PSU, CM5 + heartbeat) and the bench instruments in use; colours mark what the step is about, what is energised, the injected fault, instruments and restored parts; fully translated (Hebrew labels + captions)

DVT: figures are generated from dvt_tool/figures.py (element states per test + per-step overrides, one machine, one legend); python -m dvt_tool.figures exports SVG (docs/figures); pytest refuses a catalog test without a figure and checks every label has a translation; QA-tool mirror test

DVT: temperature by component, per machine (SRS-DVT-195) — every recorded temperature (°C fields, sweep values included) grouped by the component it measures (LED panel right / left / back / door, heater body, chamber, ambient) with n / mean / std / min / max per machine, between-machine std and spread, and outlier machines (mean further from the median of the machines than 3x the scaled MAD, 2x the pooled within-machine std and 2 °C, whichever is largest; >= 3 machines — one hot machine cannot drag the reference, an even spread never flags)

DVT Statistics page: new card 'Temperature by component — machine comparison' — component filter, table (mean ± std per machine, between-unit std, spread, outliers in red) and a mean ± std chart per selected row; Reports page: 'Temperature graphs →' button

DVT exports (every sync to Drive): temperature_by_component.csv, 'TempStats' sheet in the workbook (outlier rows highlighted), a 'Temperature by component' section in the report with the per-component summary, and charts/temp_<component>.png (matplotlib, mean ± std per machine)

DVT: dvt_tool/tempstats.py (pure logic), SRS-DVT-Tool requirement 195, compliance rows (095 now Met), README; pytest: component mapping + outlier rule, collect/export end-to-end; QA: 'DVT Temperature By Component · Per-Machine Std + Outliers' mirror test

DVT wizard fix: on the Done page (run finished — PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/WAIVED) the Back button was disabled and Leave/Next hidden, so the operator had no way out of the finished run; Back is now enabled on every stage after the first and on Done it reads 'Back to console' and leaves the wizard (the console then shows the next action for the unit); Hebrew label; QA wizard-gating test extended with the footer mirror

DVT console: fits the screen — the 1500x920 design is clamped to the work area, opens maximised in a compact layout (narrow rail, short title) when the logical screen is smaller (1920x1080 at 150 % = 1280x688), every page scrolls vertically instead of being cut off, dialogs clamped too (dvt_tool/ui/screen.py)
DVT dashboard: 'Progress by machine' — one progress bar per unit under test with committed/applicable runs (rejected excluded), failed count and the current phase
QA: 'Progress Bar Per Machine' mirror test; pytest: unit progress + screen fit

DVT catalog v0.18: new test DVT-THM-004 — heater over-drive on 230 V mains with the voltage selector at 110 V (the DVT-SAF-001 fault), timed: the heater shutdown is the branch fuse opening, read as the rise-to-fall turn on the heater-body thermocouple (PicoLog TC-08); heater_off_time = HEAT command to that turn, recorded with the body temperature at the turn, the body peak, which fuse opened, the software's reaction and a functional heat-up afterwards; SINGLE on UUT-05 in the Destructive phase, may share the energisation with SAF-001; manual mains abort at the 250 C body ceiling is a FAIL

DVT catalog: new heater_thresholds block — body_ceiling 250 C (CONFIRM, the SAF-013 manual abort ceiling) and selector_mismatch_fuse_open_max (CONFIRM, null -> the THM-004 verdict is BLOCKED until decided); the catalog loader exposes it to pass criteria; Hebrew overlay, verification plan (phase rows, method note, open decision), pytest criteria test and QA-tool mirror

DVT catalog v0.17: new test DVT-SAF-021 — voltage selector in the mid position (open circuit): the heater receives no power, the heater-body thermocouple must stay flat, the system must detect 'no heating' within a bounded time and the alarm must tell the customer to set the selector to the position matching their country's mains. 30 tests / 406 runs; Hebrew overlay, plan doc, README, tests
DVT simulator: 'Voltage selector in the mid position' fault + 60 s no-heating watchdog (Err 7004) whose guidance names the selector
Error registry: Err 7004 (temperature stall) guidance now tells the customer to check the voltage selector detent (230 V / 115 V) — a mid position is an open circuit
QA: 'DVT-SAF-021 · No-Heating Alarm Tells The Customer To Set The Voltage Selector' readiness test

DVT-SAF-007 (LED thermistor open circuit) step 3 is now instrumented with the Ophir StarBright: 'Measure with the Ophir meter…' switches the LEDs on at maximum, waits for a stable reading, prompts the operator to pull the selected thermistor's connector (in simulation the open-thermistor fault is injected), records irradiance vs time until the UV is gone, switches the LEDs off and attaches the CSV + graph; led_off_time = disconnection (first machine poll with that LED reading null, or the operator marker) to irradiance below 10 % of plateau, verdict against the 2 s limit; fills led_off_time, sensor_position, alarm_raised, alarm_identifies_sensor (alarm text names the position), error_code

DVT: the UV-off runner is trigger-generic (door for SAF-012, LED thermistor for SAF-007) — catalog step key tool: led_off_timing, CSV/PNG artefacts carry the trigger and the test's limit; catalog v0.16 (SAF-007 equipment, preconditions, Hebrew overlay), verification plan note, pytest + QA-tool mirror tests

DVT catalog v0.15: heater shutdown is proven on the heater-body thermocouple (PicoLog TC-08) in every test that expects the heater to be cut — SAF-003 rewritten (fan failure injected during heat-up at full output; heater_off_time = disconnection to the rise-to-fall turn on the trace; heater_body_drop_observed in the criteria), SAF-014 rewritten (heater SSR off read on the heater body, LED SSR off read on the Ophir StarBright trace), SAF-015 (no auto-resume proven by the trace staying in fall for 2 min after mains returns); SAF-004/005/013 already used the method
DVT: Hebrew overlay, verification plan (rows + method note) and tests updated

DVT catalog v0.14: DVT-SAF-005 redefined — the heater control NTC is replaced by a fixed 10 kOhm resistor (10 kOhm @ 25 C, beta 3934 -> a constant, plausible 25 C reading that no range check can catch). With HEAT commanded the software must, within 3 minutes of a reading that does not respond to full heater output, raise an error naming the temperature reading, switch the heater off immediately (timestamped on the heater-body thermocouple, TC-08) and refuse every further HEAT command until the sensor is fixed and acknowledged

DVT-SAF-005 criteria: alarm <= 180 s, alarm names the temperature reading, heater off at the alarm (<= 2 s), HEAT inhibited and fault re-reported while the resistor is fitted, thermal cutout must NOT have had to act (cutout acting = detection failed), chamber <= 95 C, normal heat-up after the NTC is refitted; proposed firmware rule recorded as CONFIRM (demand >= 90 % for 180 s with < 1 C change -> alarm) — the same rule detects a tripped cutout (SAF-013) and under-power (SAF-011)
DVT: Hebrew overlay, verification plan, criteria test and the SAF-005 readiness QA test updated to the fixed-resistor procedure

DVT catalog v0.13: DVT-SAF-004 (heater sensor open circuit) — heater_off_time is now read from the type-K thermocouple bonded to the heater body and logged by the PicoLog TC-08 (the same bond as SAF-013): the instant the heater-body trace turns from rising to falling is the de-energisation, the time from pulling the sensor connector to that turn is heater_off_time; the TC-08 clock is the time base and the log is attached

DVT-SAF-004 precondition changed: the sensor is pulled during heat-up with the heater at full output (not at steady state, where PID duty-cycling would blur the turn); new fields disconnect_timestamp, heater_temp_at_disconnect, heater_body_drop_observed, heater_temp_peak, raw_log_attached; criteria require a visible rise-to-fall turn; catalog note: the trace method is conservative (bond lag), a trace FAIL is cross-checked electrically before it is recorded
DVT: Hebrew overlay, verification plan and criteria test updated

DVT: Ophir StarBright power meter connected to the console (dvt_tool/instruments/ophir.py) — StarLab USB COM object, RS-232/USB-serial ($SP polling, CONFIRM against the manual), or a simulated meter for rehearsal

DVT-SAF-012 step 2 is now instrumented: 'Measure with the Ophir meter…' switches the LEDs on at maximum, waits for a stable reading, opens the door (API release or operator prompt), records irradiance vs time until the UV is gone, switches the LEDs off, and attaches the CSV + graph (door-open / UV-off markers, uv_off_time vs the 1 s limit) to the run; fills uv_off_time, residual_irradiance, alarm_raised, error_code
DVT simulator: opening the door cuts UV instantly (hardware interlock) and raises the door alarm
DVT catalog: SAF-012 equipment (Ophir StarBright + head fixture), Hebrew overlay updated; requirements: pyserial, matplotlib (pywin32 optional)
QA: 'SAF-012 UV-Off Analysis (Ophir trace)' mirror test; pytest: UV-off sequence against the simulator, pure analysis, catalog instrumentation

DVT catalog v0.12: DVT-SAF-013 (independent thermal cutout) rewritten as the operator asked — type-K thermocouple bonded to the heater body at the cutout and logged by the PicoLog TC-08, heater commanded at 100% continuously with EVERY software temperature limit removed (the cutout must be the only device able to stop heating), and the two characterisation numbers recorded: heater-body temperature at which the cutout opens and time from heater-on to the trip

DVT-SAF-013 evidence and guards: chamber time-to-peak / overshoot / cooling rate after the trip (a falling chamber under a 100% heater command is the software-visible proof that power was removed); heater_command_percent >= 100 and no manual mains abort guard that the run was really unlimited; trip judged within +/-10 C of the cutout's rated temperature (CONFIRM); software limits must be restored and verified afterwards; safety plan with a manual abort ceiling (CONFIRM 250 C on the heater body)

DVT-SAF-013 expected finding recorded in the catalog: the controller has no cutout input and no heater-response watchdog in HEAT, so alarm_raised fails on the machine as built — a software requirement (heater-response watchdog or cutout auxiliary contact), not a waiver
DVT: Hebrew overlay, verification plan and tests updated; QA: 'DVT-SAF-013 · Thermal Cutout Under Unlimited Heating' test

DVT catalog v0.11: DVT-ELE-005 now sweeps mains voltage 100 / 110 / 230 / 240 V (100 V added as the low-line point on the 110 V selector position) — one run per voltage, 20 runs across 5 units (was 15); 401 applicable runs in the campaign

DVT-ELE-005 records input power per operating mode — idle, heater only (HEAT), LEDs only (CURE without heating) and the whole machine working (heater at full output + all four LED drivers) — with current and power factor for each; the whole-machine figure is the rating-label number

DVT-ELE-005 pass criteria: recording plausibility (whole-machine power >= heater-only and >= CURE-only) and inrush repeated >= 3 switch-ons inside the run; Hebrew overlay, verification plan and tests updated

DVT store: the run set is reconciled with the catalog at start-up — runs a re-shaped test no longer defines are removed when never started and kept (and listed in the campaign events) when they hold data, so a catalog change no longer leaves stale runs in the campaign totals
QA: 'DVT-ELE-005 · Power Per Mode x Mains Voltage' test

DVT console: in Hebrew everything is Hebrew, in English everything is English (SRS-DVT-194) — the catalog prose the operator reads (test titles, purposes, sample rationale, safety plans, equipment, preconditions, procedure steps, case descriptions, phase names/gates, unit roles, subsystem and method names) now follows the console language via the overlay catalog/DVT_test_catalog.he.yaml, applied by Catalog.load(path, lang); identifiers (test ids, field names, enum values, verdicts, pass criteria, calibration keys, run ids) never change

DVT tests: overlay covers all 29 tests with Hebrew prose and identical identifiers / run ids; mismatch refusal; engine messages follow the language
QA: 'DVT Catalog Language Overlay' test

Cure process: the Pause button on the active phase card is now white with a 2 px outline in the current state's color (heating orange, drying blue, cure purple, cooling teal, bleaching cyan) — the same color as the card border

QA: 'Pause Button: White + State-Color Outline' and 'Slide-To-Start Cure Control' tests

Damper servo (MG90S, GPIO8): pulses are now hardware-timed by the CM5's RP1 PIO block (new server/hardware/pio_servo helper + build-pio-servo.sh) instead of software-timed lgpio PWM — 1 µs exact edges, no scheduling jitter, so the servo stops dead after a move instead of shivering, and no longer stops short (~45°) of open

Servo hold time 0.6 s → 1.5 s so the travel completes under load; a re-assert of the same position after release re-drives the servo (a stalled servo used to be ignored until the damper was cycled); releases always finish the pulse in flight
components.json servo.driver auto|pio|lgpio (auto = PIO when available, lgpio fallback); /api/state.damperDriver reports which is active; `io_controller.py servo` prints the driver
QA: 'Damper Servo: Hardware-Timed Pulses (PIO)' test

HDT calibration end-of-run summary: next to the recommended system LED power, the software now reports the 'boost' time — how long the model needs at 90% calibrated power to go from 35°C to the lower HDT limit (HDT − safety margin); measured from the 90% step when possible, otherwise estimated from a first-order thermal model fitted to the tested levels (marked 'estimated'); included in the HTML report
QA: 'HDT Boost Time Figure' test

HDT calibration: no cooling step between power levels any more — the next level is applied directly with the LEDs staying on (NEXT_STEP_MAX_TEMP_DELTA_C default 0 = off; a value > 0 restores the cooling gate)

HDT calibration: new stability criterion 'Max Rate' (°C/min) — the averaged temperature's slope over the stability window must also be ≤ X °C/min (default 0.5, 0 = off); Stability Band, Stability Time and Max Rate are now editable on the HDT screen before a run, and the live rate is shown while running
QA: 'HDT Rate-Of-Change Criterion' test

HDT calibration: the heater fan stays at 100% even after a heater OFF — the heater-fan run-on (30% then all-fans-off) is cancelled when the run starts and the 100% duty is re-commanded every 5 s for the whole run; released to 0% at the end

PicoLog TC-08: the usbtc08 driver is also looked up in local driver dirs (/opt/picoscope/lib, ~/pico/root/opt/picoscope/lib, SCURE_TC08_LIB_DIR) — picosdk only consults the system loader cache, so a libusbtc08 .deb extracted with dpkg -x (no sudo) now works; test machine: TC-08 S/N AO114/209 connected

HDT calibration: the chamber heater fan runs at 100% for the whole run (HDT_HEATER_FAN_PWM) and is released to 0% on every exit path (complete / abort / HDT limit / sensor error); status publishes heaterFanPwm
QA: 'HDT Heater Fan 100%' test

QA tool: new 'Developer Mode' test category — dev-mode entry logic (10 presses / PIN 8176 / OFF after restart), LED factor persistence round-trip, calibrated system-power scaling (50% → 50.0/46.0/48.5/47.5, clamp at 100%), PicoLog TC-08 status fields, HDT start gate + default constants, and HDT recommendation logic (highest PASS ≤ HDT − margin)
Cure/Bleaching steps can now run WITHOUT chamber heating: 'Chamber Heating: Off (UV only)' in the step editor and the program builder — the heater stays off, UV and the step timer start immediately

No-heat UV steps get a 'Ventilation' option: On opens the damper and runs the chamber intake fan (fresh outside air, the same airflow path as cooling) for the whole UV exposure; released automatically at step end / stop / abort / next step
Ventilation fan duty configurable via components.json ventilation.fan_pwm (default 60%)
CSV format: Temperature 'off' on a Cure/Bleaching row = no heating; new 'Ventilation' column (on/off)

LED intensity calibration: independent Back/Door/Left/Right factors (persisted on the machine); one logical 'calibrated system LED power' drives all four zones through the factors everywhere — cure, diagnostics, HDT

Material HDT calibration: automatic 10–90% system-power sweep against the entered material HDT, measured on a PicoLog TC-08 (CH1) — moving average, 2°C/5min stability detection, 30 min timeout, hard HDT stop, recommended power = highest stabilized level at or below HDT minus safety margin
Live HDT screen: PicoLog/CH1 status gate, live temperature graph with HDT lines and power transitions, abort at any time; CSV + HTML report export (USB first), partial runs preserved
Safety: PicoLog disconnect, invalid/stale CH1 data, abort or any internal error force all four LED zones to the existing safe OFF state
Timestamped Developer Mode event log (server journal + server/data/dev_events.jsonl)
